nodes.title: Vector space
nodes.body: A set $V$ with vector addition and scalar multiplication over a field $F$, satisfying the vector-space axioms. Its elements need not be arrows or lists.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: A specified scalar field F and specified operations.

nodes.title: Vector
nodes.body: An element $v\in V$. A polynomial, function, matrix or coordinate tuple can be a vector when its ambient vector space is specified.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Scalar multiplication
nodes.body: The action $(a,v)\mapsto av$ of $F$ on $V$. Scaling a coordinate list is one representation of this operation.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Linear combination
nodes.body: A finite sum $a_1v_1+\cdots+a_nv_n$. The coefficients and the selected vectors have different semantic roles even when both are displayed as numbers.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Span
nodes.body: $\operatorname{span}(v_1,\ldots,v_k)$ is the set of all linear combinations of the listed vectors.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Subspace
nodes.body: A subset $U\subseteq V$ containing zero and closed under addition and scalar multiplication, with the inherited operations.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Linear independence
nodes.body: A list is linearly independent when $\sum_i a_iv_i=0$ forces every $a_i=0$. Dependence concerns the entire list, not a property of an isolated nonzero vector.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Ordered basis
nodes.body: An ordered list $\mathcal B=(b_1,\ldots,b_n)$ that spans $V$ and is linearly independent. The order matters for coordinates.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: Finite-dimensional V for this finite-list presentation.

nodes.title: Dimension
nodes.body: The number of vectors in any basis of a finite-dimensional space. Equality of basis sizes is a theorem, not an arbitrary display convention.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: Finite-dimensional vector space.

nodes.title: Coordinates in a basis
nodes.body: $[v]_{\mathcal B}=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)^T$ means $v=\sum_i a_ib_i$. Changing the basis changes this list without changing $v$.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Polynomial as a vector
nodes.body: For $p=a_0+a_1x+a_2x^2+a_3x^3$, the coefficient column is $[p]_{(1,x,x^2,x^3)}=(a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3)^T$. The symbols being removed in a view still identify basis vectors in the semantic model.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: Formal polynomials of degree at most 3 over F, including the zero polynomial.

nodes.title: Linear map
nodes.body: $T:V\to W$ satisfies $T(u+v)=T(u)+T(v)$ and $T(av)=aT(v)$. Domain, codomain and scalar field are part of its context.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: V and W are vector spaces over the same field.

nodes.title: Matrix
nodes.body: An $m\times n$ array over $F$. It can encode a linear map in chosen bases, a system of equations, or a collection of vectors; those roles are additional context.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Matrix of a linear map
nodes.body: $[T]_{\mathcal C\leftarrow\mathcal B}$ has column $j$ equal to $[T(b_j)]_{\mathcal C}$. It satisfies $[T(v)]_{\mathcal C}=[T]_{\mathcal C\leftarrow\mathcal B}[v]_{\mathcal B}$.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: Finite-dimensional domain and codomain; ordered bases B and C.

nodes.title: Matrix row
nodes.body: Row $i$ of $A$ records the coefficients of the $i$th output coordinate functional. As a list it is indexed by input coordinates.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Matrix column
nodes.body: Column $j$ of a matrix representing $T$ is the coordinate vector of $T(b_j)$. It is indexed by output coordinates.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Covector / linear functional
nodes.body: A linear map $\varphi:V\to F$. A row of coefficients represents it after choosing a basis. The pairing $\varphi(v)$ needs no inner product.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Dual space
nodes.body: $V^*=\operatorname{Hom}(V,F)$, the vector space of linear functionals on $V$. An identification of $V$ with $V^*$ requires extra choices or structure.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Covector–vector evaluation
nodes.body: $\varphi(v)=\sum_i\varphi(b_i)[v]_{\mathcal B,i}$. This is bilinear over $F$. It differs from a complex inner product, which conjugates one argument.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: Matching basis and dual-coordinate convention.

nodes.title: Matrix–vector product
nodes.body: $Ax=\sum_jx_jA_{:,j}$. Its $i$th entry is the evaluation of row $i$ on $x$. These are two presentations of one product.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: A is m×n; x has n coordinates.

nodes.title: Matrix multiplication
nodes.body: For $A\in F^{m\times n}$ and $B\in F^{n\times p}$, $(AB)_{ij}=\sum_k A_{ik}B_{kj}$. Rows, columns, entries and both factor maps must remain addressable within this one object.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: Matching inner dimension n; compatible intermediate coordinates.

nodes.title: Composition of linear maps
nodes.body: For $S:U\to V$ and $T:V\to W$, $(T\circ S)(u)=T(S(u))$. The rightmost map acts first.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: The output of S is in the domain of T.

nodes.title: Outer-product expansion
nodes.body: $AB=\sum_k A_{:,k}B_{k,:}$. Each summand is a column times a row, producing an $m\times p$ matrix of rank at most one.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: A is m×n; B is n×p; expansion follows entrywise.

nodes.title: Linear system
nodes.body: $Ax=b$ asks for all input coordinates that produce the chosen output. It can be read as simultaneous equations, a column combination, or a preimage under a map.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Gaussian elimination
nodes.body: Invertible elementary row operations transform an augmented system while preserving its solution set. The numerical coefficient matrix changes.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Elementary matrix
nodes.body: Applying a single elementary row operation to the identity produces $E$. Left multiplication by $E$ applies that row operation.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Reduced row-echelon form
nodes.body: A row-echelon matrix whose pivots are 1 and are the only nonzero entries in their columns. RREF is unique within a row-equivalence class.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Kernel / null space
nodes.body: $\ker T=\{v:T(v)=0\}$. It is a subspace of the domain. Matrix null-space coordinates depend on the input basis.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Image / range
nodes.body: $\operatorname{im}T=\{T(v):v\in V\}$. For $x\mapsto Ax$ in standard coordinates this is the span of the columns of $A$. The codomain may be larger.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Preimage / solution fiber
nodes.body: $T^{-1}(b)=\{v:T(v)=b\}$. If nonempty and $T$ is linear, it equals $v_0+\ker T$ for any one solution $v_0$. It need not be a subspace.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Rank
nodes.body: $\operatorname{rank}T=\dim(\operatorname{im}T)$. For a matrix this equals column rank and row rank.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Injectivity
nodes.body: $T(u)=T(v)$ implies $u=v$. A linear map is injective exactly when its kernel is zero.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Surjectivity
nodes.body: Every element of the specified codomain is attained. Surjectivity is equality of image and codomain, so the codomain cannot be omitted from the object.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Identity
nodes.body: $I_V(v)=v$. In matching input and output bases its matrix is the identity matrix. Its columns show the original basis vectors unchanged.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Inverse
nodes.body: For a bijective linear map $T$, the inverse $T^{-1}$ satisfies $T^{-1}T=I$ and $TT^{-1}=I$. A left inverse alone is insufficient for arbitrary rectangular maps.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Change of basis
nodes.body: If $P$ has columns $[c_j]_{\mathcal B}$, then $[v]_{\mathcal B}=P[v]_{\mathcal C}$. This changes coordinates, not the underlying vector.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Similarity
nodes.body: $B=P^{-1}AP$ with $P$ invertible. These matrices can represent the same endomorphism in two bases.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Eigenvector and eigenvalue
nodes.body: $Tv=\lambda v$ with $v\ne0$. The invariant direction is essential; the zero vector is excluded even though it satisfies the equation for every scalar.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: T is an endomorphism V→V; λ belongs to the chosen scalar field.

nodes.title: Eigenspace
nodes.body: $E_\lambda=\ker(T-\lambda I)$. It includes zero; its nonzero vectors are the eigenvectors for $\lambda$.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Diagonalization
nodes.body: $A=PDP^{-1}$ where $D$ is diagonal. The columns of $P$ are a basis of eigenvectors, and the corresponding eigenvalues are the diagonal entries of $D$.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: A square matrix over F; an eigenbasis over F exists.

nodes.title: Inner product
nodes.body: An inner product supplies lengths and angles. On $\mathbb R^n$ the standard product is $x^Ty$; on $\mathbb C^n$ a Hermitian product conjugates one argument. The argument convention must be recorded.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: Positive-definite inner product over R or C; explicitly chosen conjugate-linear slot.

nodes.title: Orthogonality
nodes.body: $u\perp v$ means $\langle u,v\rangle=0$. Without an inner product this relation is not available.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Orthonormal basis
nodes.body: A basis with $\langle q_i,q_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}$. Pairwise orthogonality alone does not imply unit length.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Orthogonal projection
nodes.body: $v=P_Uv+(v-P_Uv)$ with $P_Uv\in U$ and residual in $U^\perp$. This is a decomposition of one vector into complementary components.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: Finite-dimensional subspace U of a real or complex inner-product space.

nodes.title: Least squares
nodes.body: Minimize $\|Ax-b\|^2$. Over the reals, minimizers solve $A^T(Ax-b)=0$. The fitted vector is unique; the coefficient vector need not be.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: Real finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces; use A* over C.

nodes.title: Gram–Schmidt
nodes.body: Subtract projections onto previously constructed orthonormal directions, then normalize. Independence ensures each residual to be normalized is nonzero.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Transpose and dual map
nodes.body: $A^T$ swaps row and column indices. It represents the dual map in dual bases. A transpose is not generally the inverse.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Adjoint
nodes.body: In orthonormal bases the adjoint has matrix $A^*=\overline A^T$. With the convention linear in the first slot, $\langle Tv,w\rangle=\langle v,T^*w\rangle$.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Determinant
nodes.body: For square $A$, $\det A$ measures signed volume scaling over $\mathbb R$ and detects invertibility. It is not defined for arbitrary rectangular matrices in this sense.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: Square matrix; Euclidean oriented volume interpretation uses real coordinates.

nodes.title: Singular value decomposition
nodes.body: $A=U\Sigma V^*$ with orthonormal input and output bases and nonnegative singular values. Input and output bases may differ, unlike a similarity diagonalization.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: Finite-dimensional real or complex inner-product spaces.

nodes.title: Why row–column and column-combination views agree
nodes.body: The entry rule and the column-combination rule describe the same indexed contributions, not copied numbers that merely happen to match.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: A is m×n and B is n×p over the same field.
steps: Write the jth column of B as $b_j=\sum_k B_{kj}e_k$.
Taking output coordinate i gives $(Ab_j)_i=\sum_k A_{ik}B_{kj}$.
The columns $Ab_j$ form AB, so this is also $(AB)_{ij}$.

nodes.title: Rank–nullity
nodes.body: $\dim V=\dim\ker T+\dim\operatorname{im}T$.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: T:V→W is linear and V is finite-dimensional.
steps: Choose a basis $(u_1,\ldots,u_k)$ for $\ker T$ and extend it to a basis $(u_1,\ldots,u_k,v_1,\ldots,v_r)$ of V.
The vectors $T(v_i)$ span the image: expand any input in this basis and apply T.
If $\sum_i a_iT(v_i)=0$, then $\sum_i a_iv_i\in\ker T$. Independence of the extended basis forces every $a_i=0$.
Thus the image has basis $(T(v_1),\ldots,T(v_r))$, and $\dim V=k+r$.

nodes.title: Injectivity is a trivial kernel
nodes.body: $T$ is injective if and only if $\ker T=\{0\}$.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: T is a linear map.
steps: If T is injective and $T(v)=0=T(0)$, then $v=0$.
Conversely, $T(u)=T(v)$ implies $T(u-v)=0$. A trivial kernel forces $u-v=0$.

nodes.title: Why least squares gives normal equations
nodes.body: The residual must be orthogonal to every column of A.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: A and b are real; squared Euclidean norm.
steps: The nearest vector to b in $\operatorname{Col}(A)$ is its orthogonal projection.
Therefore $Ax-b$ is orthogonal to each column of A, exactly $A^T(Ax-b)=0$.
For such a residual and any h, $\|A(x+h)-b\|^2=\|Ax-b\|^2+\|Ah\|^2$, proving minimality.
All minimizers differ by $\ker A$; uniqueness requires full column rank.

nodes.title: Why elimination preserves solutions
nodes.body: For invertible elementary E, $Ax=b$ if and only if $EAx=Eb$.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: The same row operation is applied to both coefficient matrix and right side.
steps: Apply E to both sides of $Ax=b$ to get $EAx=Eb$.
Apply $E^{-1}$ to the transformed equation to recover $Ax=b$.
Iterate this equivalence for the sequence of elementary operations.

nodes.title: A real rotation can have no real eigenvectors
nodes.body: $R=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ has characteristic polynomial $\lambda^2+1$. It has no eigenvalues over $\mathbb R$, and eigenvalues $i,-i$ over $\mathbb C$.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
assumptions: The field changes the permitted eigenvalues and eigenvectors.

nodes.title: Vector ≠ its coordinate list
nodes.body: The polynomial $p=1+x$ has coordinates $(1,1)$ in $(1,x)$ and $(1,0)$ in $(1+x,x)$. The object p has not changed.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Row equivalence ≠ similarity
nodes.body: $I_2$ and $\operatorname{diag}(2,1)$ are row equivalent over $\mathbb R$, but are not similar: their eigenvalues differ. Elimination preserves system solutions when the right side changes too; similarity preserves the represented operator under a basis change.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Bilinear pairing ≠ Hermitian inner product
nodes.body: For $z=(1,i)^T$, $z^Tz=0$ but $z^*z=2$. Rotating a displayed column into a row cannot silently decide whether to conjugate it.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Transpose ≠ inverse
nodes.body: For $A=\operatorname{diag}(2,1)$ over $\mathbb R$, $A^T=A$ while $A^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(1/2,1)$. For real orthogonal matrices these operations do agree.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ

nodes.title: Unique fit ≠ unique coefficients
nodes.body: With $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $b=1$, every $x=(t,1-t)^T$ has zero residual. The fitted output is uniquely 1, but the coefficient vector is not unique.
nodes.context: KP research synthesis; source scopes can differ
